items.q: A soil sample has a total volume of 200 cm3 and a porosity of 45 percent. Calculate the volume of pore space in cm3.
items.s: Pore volume = total volume x porosity/100 = 200 x 45/100 = 90 cm3.

items.q: A soil sample contains 55 percent sand and 35 percent silt. Calculate the clay content in percent.
items.s: Clay = 100 - sand - silt = 100 - 55 - 35 = 10 percent.

items.q: A soil sample has a field mass of 140 g and an oven dry mass of 104 g. Calculate the gravimetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Gravimetric moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (140 - 104)/104 x 100 = 34.6 percent.

items.q: A soil takes water at a constant rate of 12 mm/h. Calculate the depth of water that enters the soil in 3 hours.
items.s: Depth infiltrated = rate x time = 12 x 3 = 36 mm.

items.q: A field of 3 hectares loses 24 tonnes of soil over 4 years. Calculate the average annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Annual loss per hectare = mass/(area x years) = 24/(3 x 4) = 2 tonnes per hectare.

items.q: A field under clean cultivation loses 120 tonnes of soil per hectare per year. With a support practice whose factor is 0.6 the loss becomes that figure multiplied by the factor. Calculate the reduced soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Reduced loss = 120 x 0.6 = 72 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: A storm delivers 30 mm of rain in 1.5 hours. Calculate the average rainfall intensity in mm/h.
items.s: Intensity = depth/duration = 30/1.5 = 20 mm/h.

items.q: At the outlet of a catchment the base flow is 0.4 m3/s and the direct storm runoff is 5 m3/s. Calculate the total stream flow in m3/s.
items.s: Total flow = base flow + direct runoff = 0.4 + 5 = 5.4 m3/s.

items.q: Ground rises 3 m over a horizontal distance of 75 m. Calculate the land slope in percent.
items.s: Slope = rise/run x 100 = 3/75 x 100 = 4 percent.

items.q: A gully 720 m long is to be treated with check dams spaced 60 m apart, with one at the head of the gully. Calculate the number of check dams required.
items.s: Intervals = gully length/spacing = 720/60 = 12, so the number of check dams including the one at the head is 12 + 1 = 13.

items.q: A field is graded so that it falls 0.9 m along a run of 250 m. Calculate the graded slope in percent.
items.s: Graded slope = fall/run x 100 = 0.9/250 x 100 = 0.36 percent.

items.q: A farm pond is designed to hold water to a depth of 1.5 m and must be given a freeboard of 0.2 m. Calculate the height of the embankment in m.
items.s: Embankment height = water depth + freeboard = 1.5 + 0.2 = 1.7 m.

items.q: A field 160 m wide is to be drained by parallel field drains spaced 20 m apart, with a drain along each edge. Calculate the number of drain lines required.
items.s: Intervals = width/spacing = 160/20 = 8, so the number of lines with one on each edge is 8 + 1 = 9.

items.q: A shelterbelt is planted with trees 12 m tall and a spacing rule of 20 times the tree height is used. Calculate the spacing between shelterbelts in m.
items.s: Spacing = tree height x multiple = 12 x 20 = 240 m.

items.q: An evaporation pan loses 6 mm of water in a day and the pan coefficient for the station is 0.8. Calculate the estimated evaporation from a water surface in mm per day.
items.s: Evaporation = pan loss x pan coefficient = 6 x 0.8 = 4.8 mm per day.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.35 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.65 g/cm3. Calculate its porosity in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/particle density) x 100 = (1 - 1.35/2.65) x 100 = 49.1 percent.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.5 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.65 g/cm3. Calculate its void ratio.
items.s: Void ratio = particle density/bulk density - 1 = 2.65/1.5 - 1 = 0.767.

items.q: The solid particles in a soil sample have a mass of 166 g and occupy a volume of 75 cm3. Calculate the particle density in g/cm3.
items.s: Particle density = mass of solids/volume of solids = 166/75 = 2.21 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil has a gravimetric moisture content of 20 percent and a bulk density of 1.5 g/cm3. Taking the density of water as 1 g/cm3, calculate the volumetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Volumetric moisture = gravimetric moisture x bulk density = 20 x 1.5 = 30 percent.

items.q: A soil to a depth of 30 cm has a volumetric moisture content of 25 percent. Calculate the depth of water stored in the soil in mm.
items.s: Depth of water = volumetric moisture x depth = 0.25 x 30 cm = 7.5 cm = 75 mm.

items.q: A soil has a field capacity of 32 percent and a permanent wilting point of 12 percent by volume, with a root zone depth of 60 cm. Calculate the available water capacity in mm.
items.s: Available water = (field capacity - wilting point) x depth = (32 - 12)/100 x 60 cm = 120 mm.

items.q: A soil at field capacity holds 34 percent moisture by volume and now holds 20 percent, the root zone being 40 cm deep. Calculate the moisture deficit in mm.
items.s: Deficit = (field capacity - present moisture) x depth = (34 - 20)/100 x 40 cm = 56 mm.

items.q: A soil profile holds 55 mm of available water and the field area is 5 hectares. Calculate the total volume of available water stored in m3.
items.s: Volume = depth of water x area = 0.055 m x 50000 m2 = 2750 m3.

items.q: Water enters a soil at a steady rate of 25 mm/h over an area of 1 hectares for 6 hours. Calculate the volume of water that infiltrates in m3.
items.s: Depth entering = 25 x 6 = 150 mm, so volume = 0.15 m x 10000 m2 = 1500 m3.

items.q: Water flows at 10 cm3 per minute through a soil column of cross section 100 cm2 and length 20 cm under a head difference of 20 cm. Calculate the hydraulic conductivity in cm/min.
items.s: By Darcy law K = Q L/(A H) = 10 x 20/(100 x 20) = 0.1 cm/min.

items.q: A soil has a hydraulic conductivity of 2.5 m/day. Water seeps through a cross section of 800 m2 under a head difference of 0.5 m over a flow path of 2.5 m. Calculate the seepage discharge in m3/day.
items.s: Darcy discharge = K A i = 2.5 x 800 x (0.5/2.5) = 400 m3/day.

items.q: A canal bed of area 1000 m2 loses water into a soil of hydraulic conductivity 1.5 m/day. The water table lies so that the head gradient is 0.08. Calculate the seepage loss in m3/day.
items.s: Seepage = K A i = 1.5 x 1000 x 0.08 = 120 m3/day.

items.q: Soil loss from a catchment of 12 hectares averages 60 tonnes per hectare per year and the sediment delivery ratio is 0.4. Calculate the sediment yield at the outlet in tonnes per year.
items.s: Sediment yield = soil loss x area x delivery ratio = 60 x 12 x 0.4 = 288 tonnes per year.

items.q: A storm of 80 mm falls with an energy of 18 joules per square metre per millimetre of rain. Calculate the total kinetic energy of the storm in joules per square metre.
items.s: Storm energy = rainfall x energy per millimetre = 80 x 18 = 1440 joules per square metre.

items.q: A gully has a triangular cross section 1.2 m wide at the top and 1 m deep, and runs for 80 m. Calculate the volume of soil removed in m3.
items.s: Cross sectional area = half x width x depth = 0.5 x 1.2 x 1 = 0.6 m2, so volume = 0.6 x 80 = 48 m3.

items.q: For a field the rainfall erosivity factor is 350, the soil erodibility factor is 0.25, the combined slope factor is 3, the cover and management factor is 0.3 and the support practice factor is 0.5. Calculate the estimated annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Soil loss = R x K x LS x C x P = 350 x 0.25 x 3 x 0.3 x 0.5 = 39.38 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: The slope length factor of a field is calculated as (slope length/reference length) raised to the power 0.4, where the reference length is 25 m. For a slope length of 30 m, calculate the slope length factor.
items.s: Slope length factor = (30/25)^0.4 = 1.08.

items.q: A field loses 25 tonnes of soil per hectare per year while the soil loss tolerance for that soil is 12 tonnes per hectare per year. Calculate the ratio of actual loss to the tolerance.
items.s: Ratio = actual loss/tolerance = 25/12 = 2.08.

items.q: Each tonne of crop residue left on the surface covers 35 percent of the ground. Calculate the percentage cover left by 4 tonnes of residue per hectare.
items.s: Cover = residue x cover per tonne = 4 x 35 = 140 percent.

items.q: A storm of 40 mm on a catchment of 8 hectares produced a runoff volume of 2000 m3. Calculate the runoff coefficient.
items.s: Rainfall volume = 0.04 m x 80000 m2 = 3200 m3, so runoff coefficient = 2000/3200 = 0.62 = 0.625.

items.q: A catchment of 5 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.4. Calculate the runoff volume in m3 produced by a rainfall of 45 mm.
items.s: Runoff volume = coefficient x rainfall depth x area = 0.4 x 0.045 m x 50000 m2 = 900 m3.

items.q: A catchment of 6 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.4 and the design rainfall intensity for its time of concentration is 120 mm/h. Calculate the peak discharge by the rational method in m3/s.
items.s: Peak discharge = C x i x A/360 = 0.4 x 120 x 6/360 = 0.8 m3/s.

items.q: A storm of a stated size has a probability of 20 percent of being equalled or exceeded in any one year. Calculate its return period in years.
items.s: Return period = 100/probability = 100/20 = 5 years.

items.q: A catchment of 3 hectares produces a runoff volume of 9000 m3. Calculate the depth of runoff over the catchment in mm.
items.s: Depth = volume/area = 9000/30000 m2 = 0.3 m = 300 mm.

items.q: A runoff depth of 50 mm is produced from a catchment of 10 hectares and leaves the outlet over 6 hours. Calculate the average rate of flow in m3/s.
A field has a slope of 8 percent. Calculate the angle of the slope in degrees.
items.s: Slope angle = arctan(8/100) = 4.57 degrees.

items.q: A conservation guide sets the vertical interval between contour bunds at 1.8 m for every 10 percent of land slope. For a field with a slope of 6 percent, calculate the vertical interval in m.
items.s: Vertical interval = 1.8 x 6/10 = 1.08 m.

items.q: Contour bunds are to be laid with a vertical interval of 1.5 m on land of 12 percent slope. Calculate the horizontal spacing between bunds in m.
items.s: Horizontal spacing = vertical interval/(slope/100) = 1.5/(12/100) = 12.5 m.

items.q: A slope 90 m long is to be protected by contour bunds spaced 15 m apart horizontally, with a bund at the top of the slope. Calculate the number of bunds needed.
items.s: Intervals = length/spacing = 90/15 = 6, so the number of bunds including the top one is 6 + 1 = 7.

items.q: A contour bund has a triangular cross section 0.5 m wide at the base and 0.6 m high and is 300 m long. Calculate the volume of earth in it in m3.
items.s: Volume = half x base x height x length = 0.5 x 0.5 x 0.6 x 300 = 45 m3.

items.q: A field of 5 hectares is to be levelled by cutting an average depth of 0.15 m over the whole area. Calculate the volume of earth to be moved in m3.
items.s: Volume = area x depth = 50000 m2 x 0.15 m = 7500 m3.

items.q: A terrace bench of width 5 m is to serve an area of 0.4 hectares. Calculate the total length of terrace in m.
items.s: Length = area/width = 4000 m2/5 m = 800 m.

items.q: A drainage system must remove 12 mm of water from 6 hectares within 12 hours. Calculate the required discharge in litres per second.
items.s: Volume = 0.012 m x 60000 m2 = 720 m3, so discharge = 720 m3/(12 x 3600 s) = 16.67 litres per second.

items.q: A field drain falls 0.75 m over a length of 300 m. Calculate its gradient as a decimal fraction.
items.s: Gradient = fall/length = 0.75/300 = 0.0025, which is 0.25 percent.

items.q: A field of 2 hectares is to be underdrained with parallel drains spaced 10 m apart. Calculate the total length of drain required in m.
items.s: Total length = area/spacing = 20000 m2/10 m = 2000 m.

items.q: A drainage outlet discharges 12 litres per second for 6 hours. Calculate the total volume removed in m3.
items.s: Volume = discharge x time = 0.012 m3/s x 21600 s = 259 m3.

items.q: A grassed waterway has a Manning coefficient of 0.04, a hydraulic radius of 0.3 m and a bed slope of 0.002. Calculate the flow velocity in m/s.
A trapezoidal waterway carries water 0.4 m deep at a mean velocity of 2 m/s, its mean top width being 1.5 m. Calculate the discharge in m3/s.
items.s: Discharge = mean area x velocity = 1.5 x 0.4 x 2 = 1.2 m3/s.

items.q: A rectangular waterway is 1.5 m wide and carries water 0.5 m deep. Calculate its hydraulic radius in m.
items.s: Area = 1.5 x 0.5 = 0.75 m2 and wetted perimeter = 1.5 + 2 x 0.5 = 2.5 m, so hydraulic radius = 0.3 m.

items.q: A farm pond has a water surface area of 0.4 hectares and an average water depth of 2.5 m. Calculate its storage volume in m3.
items.s: Volume = surface area x depth = 4000 m2 x 2.5 m = 10000 m3.

items.q: A farmer needs to store 300 m3 of water from a catchment that receives 400 mm of rain a year, with a runoff efficiency of 0.5. Calculate the catchment area needed in hectares.
items.s: Yield per hectare = 0.4 m x 0.5 = 0.2 m3, so area = 300/0.2 = 0.15 hectares.

items.q: A soil core of volume 200 cm3 has an oven dry mass of 492 g. Calculate the bulk density in g/cm3.
items.s: Bulk density = oven dry mass/volume = 492/200 = 2.46 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil sample has a total volume of 300 cm3 and a porosity of 52 percent. Calculate the volume of pore space in cm3.
items.s: Pore volume = total volume x porosity/100 = 300 x 52/100 = 156 cm3.

items.q: A soil sample contains 36 percent sand and 21 percent silt. Calculate the clay content in percent.
items.s: Clay = 100 - sand - silt = 100 - 36 - 21 = 43 percent.

items.q: A soil sample has a field mass of 150 g and an oven dry mass of 94 g. Calculate the gravimetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Gravimetric moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (150 - 94)/94 x 100 = 59.6 percent.

items.q: The statement “the oven dry mass of soil divided by the total volume it occupies, pores included” describes which of the following?
o: aggregate
soil colour
bulk density
hardpan
items.s: bulk density is the oven dry mass of soil divided by the total volume it occupies, pores included.

items.q: The statement “the quantity of soil that must be moved to bring a field to its planned level” describes which of the following?
o: freeboard
bund
earthwork volume
land grading
items.s: earthwork volume is the quantity of soil that must be moved to bring a field to its planned level.

items.q: Which term is described by “the amount by which the water present in the root zone falls short of field capacity”?
o: saturation
volumetric moisture content
moisture deficit
hygroscopic water
items.s: moisture deficit is the amount by which the water present in the root zone falls short of field capacity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes drain spacing?
o: the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow
the distance measured along the ground between successive conservation ridges
the distance between parallel field drains
the volume of water held in a soil expressed as a fraction of the total soil volume
items.s: drain spacing: the distance between parallel field drains. The other options describe rill erosion, volumetric moisture content, horizontal spacing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines water table.
o: the upper surface of the zone in which the soil pores are full of water
a levelled or gently sloping bench cut into a hillside for cultivation
a cluster of soil particles held together by clay, organic matter or root action
a channel built above a cultivated area to divert water coming from higher ground
items.s: water table: the upper surface of the zone in which the soil pores are full of water. The other options describe terrace, cut off drain, aggregate.

items.q: Which of the following best describes riser?
o: an unlined channel drawn through the subsoil by a bullet shaped implement
the steep face between one terrace bench and the next
moisture held so tightly by soil particles that plants cannot absorb it
a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the length of uninterrupted slope increases
items.s: riser: the steep face between one terrace bench and the next. The other options describe slope length factor, hygroscopic water, mole drain.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines soil profile.
o: the depth of rain falling in unit time during a storm
the point at which a drain discharges its water into a natural stream or channel
the vertical arrangement of distinct layers seen in a cut through the soil
a levelled or gently sloping bench cut into a hillside for cultivation
items.s: soil profile: the vertical arrangement of distinct layers seen in a cut through the soil. The other options describe terrace, rainfall intensity, outlet.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines contour line.
o: the condition in which the pore space of the root zone stays filled with water
a line drawn on the ground joining points of equal elevation
the volume of water held in a soil expressed as a fraction of the total soil volume
the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet
items.s: contour line: a line drawn on the ground joining points of equal elevation. The other options describe waterlogging, volumetric moisture content, sediment delivery ratio.

items.q: Which term is described by “the enlargement of rills into deep channels that cannot be crossed by farm machinery”?
o: gully erosion
sheet erosion
soil loss tolerance
splash erosion
items.s: gully erosion is the enlargement of rills into deep channels that cannot be crossed by farm machinery.

items.q: Which term is described by “the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water”?
o: bund
cut and fill
terrace channel
land grading
items.s: terrace channel is the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water.

items.q: Which of the following best describes water table?
o: the upper surface of the zone in which the soil pores are full of water
the oven dry mass of soil divided by the total volume it occupies, pores included
the slow movement of stored water into or through the soil of a pond or channel
the moisture level at which a plant can no longer draw water and wilts beyond recovery
items.s: water table: the upper surface of the zone in which the soil pores are full of water. The other options describe bulk density, seepage, permanent wilting point.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines soil loss tolerance.
o: the reshaping of a field surface to a planned slope by cutting and filling
the downward movement of water through the soil body below the surface layer
the formation of a thin hard skin at the soil surface that resists the entry of water
the greatest rate of erosion that a soil can suffer without losing productivity
items.s: soil loss tolerance: the greatest rate of erosion that a soil can suffer without losing productivity. The other options describe land grading, crusting, percolation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines evaporation pan?
o: a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss where conservation works are in place
an open vessel of water exposed to the air whose loss of water indicates the evaporating power of the weather
a small barrier across a gully that slows the flow and traps sediment
the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period
items.s: evaporation pan: an open vessel of water exposed to the air whose loss of water indicates the evaporating power of the weather. The other options describe sediment yield, check dam, support practice factor.

items.q: Which term is described by “an unlined channel drawn through the subsoil by a bullet shaped implement”?
o: outlet
mole drain
drain spacing
water table
items.s: mole drain is an unlined channel drawn through the subsoil by a bullet shaped implement.

items.q: Which term is described by “the water held between field capacity and the wilting point that a crop can use”?
o: available water
moisture deficit
root zone depth
permanent wilting point
items.s: available water is the water held between field capacity and the wilting point that a crop can use.

items.q: Which of the following best describes aggregate?
o: the lifting, sorting and carrying away of dry loose soil by moving air
the mass of the solid particles of a soil divided by the volume of those solids alone
a cluster of soil particles held together by clay, organic matter or root action
the state in which every pore in the soil is filled with water
items.s: aggregate: a cluster of soil particles held together by clay, organic matter or root action. The other options describe wind erosion, particle density, saturation.

items.q: land grading may be defined as
o: the reshaping of a field surface to a planned slope by cutting and filling
the fraction of the rainfall on a catchment that appears as surface flow
the depth of soil through which the roots of a crop draw their water
a small barrier across a gully that slows the flow and traps sediment
items.s: land grading: the reshaping of a field surface to a planned slope by cutting and filling. The other options describe root zone depth, check dam, runoff coefficient.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Darcy law?
o: the statement that the flow through a porous material is proportional to the head gradient and the cross section
the state in which every pore in the soil is filled with water
the depth of water that a drainage system is designed to remove in a stated time
the enlargement of rills into deep channels that cannot be crossed by farm machinery
items.s: Darcy law: the statement that the flow through a porous material is proportional to the head gradient and the cross section. The other options describe saturation, drainage coefficient, gully erosion.

items.q: Which of the following best describes return period?
o: tillage that leaves crop residue on the surface to shield the soil
the average number of years between storms that equal or exceed a stated size
the entry of water into the soil surface from rain or applied water
the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet
items.s: return period: the average number of years between storms that equal or exceed a stated size. The other options describe sediment delivery ratio, infiltration, conservation tillage.

items.q: sediment delivery ratio may be defined as
o: the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet
the shade of a soil used as an indicator of drainage, organic matter and mineral content
the depth of water that enters the soil in unit time
the arrangement of individual soil particles into groups or aggregates
items.s: sediment delivery ratio: the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet. The other options describe infiltration rate, soil colour, soil structure.

items.q: freeboard may be defined as
o: the removal of a thin fairly uniform layer of soil over a whole slope
the mass of water held in a soil expressed as a percentage of the oven dry mass of that soil
the fraction of the rainfall on a catchment that appears as surface flow
the height left between the design water level and the top of an embankment
items.s: freeboard: the height left between the design water level and the top of an embankment. The other options describe sheet erosion, runoff coefficient, gravimetric moisture content.

items.q: Which of the following best describes farm pond?
o: the height difference between one conservation ridge and the next down the slope
the balanced shifting of soil from high spots to low spots during grading
an earth ridge built along the contour to hold water and trap soil
a small excavated or embanked reservoir that stores runoff for later use
items.s: farm pond: a small excavated or embanked reservoir that stores runoff for later use. The other options describe vertical interval, contour bund, cut and fill.

items.q: Which of the following best describes contour ploughing?
o: the volume of water held in a soil expressed as a fraction of the total soil volume
the removal of water that stands on or flows over the land surface
ploughing along the contour so that each furrow checks the downslope movement of water
the oven dry mass of soil divided by the total volume it occupies, pores included
items.s: contour ploughing: ploughing along the contour so that each furrow checks the downslope movement of water. The other options describe volumetric moisture content, surface drainage, bulk density.

items.q: Which term is described by “a compacted layer in the soil that roots and water penetrate only with difficulty”?
o: hardpan
particle density
soil texture
soil colour
items.s: hardpan is a compacted layer in the soil that roots and water penetrate only with difficulty.

items.q: terrace channel may be defined as
o: the enlargement of rills into deep channels that cannot be crossed by farm machinery
a value showing how readily a particular soil is lost under a standard set of conditions
the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water
the removal of water that stands on or flows over the land surface
items.s: terrace channel: the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water. The other options describe soil erodibility factor, gully erosion, surface drainage.

items.q: Which of the following best describes runoff coefficient?
o: the mass of water held in a soil expressed as a percentage of the oven dry mass of that soil
the point at which a drain discharges its water into a natural stream or channel
the amount by which the water present in the root zone falls short of field capacity
the fraction of the rainfall on a catchment that appears as surface flow
items.s: runoff coefficient: the fraction of the rainfall on a catchment that appears as surface flow. The other options describe outlet, gravimetric moisture content, moisture deficit.

items.q: Which of the following best describes terrace channel?
o: the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water
the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet
the part of stream flow that comes from ground water rather than direct storm runoff
the length of channel boundary in contact with flowing water
items.s: terrace channel: the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water. The other options describe base flow, sediment delivery ratio, wetted perimeter.

items.q: peak discharge may be defined as
o: an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet
the depth of water that a drainage system is designed to remove in a stated time
the greatest rate of flow reached at a point during or after a storm
the time taken for water to travel from the farthest point of a catchment to its outlet
items.s: peak discharge: the greatest rate of flow reached at a point during or after a storm. The other options describe drainage coefficient, graded bund, time of concentration.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines porosity?
o: moisture held so tightly by soil particles that plants cannot absorb it
a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss according to the crop and its residue
the steep face between one terrace bench and the next
the share of the total soil volume that is occupied by air and water
items.s: porosity: the share of the total soil volume that is occupied by air and water. The other options describe cover and management factor, riser, hygroscopic water.

items.q: Which term is described by “a row or belt of trees planted to slow the wind over nearby land”?
o: shelterbelt
evaporation pan
wetted perimeter
water harvesting
items.s: shelterbelt is a row or belt of trees planted to slow the wind over nearby land.

items.q: The statement “the amount by which the water present in the root zone falls short of field capacity” describes which of the following?
o: gravimetric moisture content
available water
volumetric moisture content
moisture deficit
items.s: moisture deficit is the amount by which the water present in the root zone falls short of field capacity.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines contour line?
o: the depth of water that a drainage system is designed to remove in a stated time
the mass of the solid particles of a soil divided by the volume of those solids alone
the moisture level at which a plant can no longer draw water and wilts beyond recovery
a line drawn on the ground joining points of equal elevation
items.s: contour line: a line drawn on the ground joining points of equal elevation. The other options describe permanent wilting point, drainage coefficient, particle density.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines saturation?
o: the state in which every pore in the soil is filled with water
the susceptibility of a soil to being detached and carried away by erosive agents
a compacted layer in the soil that roots and water penetrate only with difficulty
the height difference between one conservation ridge and the next down the slope
items.s: saturation: the state in which every pore in the soil is filled with water. The other options describe hardpan, erodibility, vertical interval.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines sediment yield?
o: the amount by which the water present in the root zone falls short of field capacity
the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water
the average number of years between storms that equal or exceed a stated size
the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period
items.s: sediment yield: the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period. The other options describe moisture deficit, terrace channel, return period.

items.q: Which term is described by “an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet”?
o: grassed waterway
contour bund
graded bund
horizontal spacing
items.s: graded bund is an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ease with which water moves through a soil under a pressure difference”?
o: hydraulic conductivity
permeability
crusting
preferential flow
items.s: permeability is the ease with which water moves through a soil under a pressure difference.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines field capacity.
o: the formation of a thin hard skin at the soil surface that resists the entry of water
moisture held so tightly by soil particles that plants cannot absorb it
the moisture left in a soil after free drainage has ceased following thorough wetting
an open vessel of water exposed to the air whose loss of water indicates the evaporating power of the weather
items.s: field capacity: the moisture left in a soil after free drainage has ceased following thorough wetting. The other options describe hygroscopic water, crusting, evaporation pan.

items.q: rainfall erosivity factor may be defined as
o: the condition in which the pore space of the root zone stays filled with water
an index of the combined effect of rainfall amount and intensity on soil loss
a low earth embankment thrown up to hold back water or soil
an open vessel of water exposed to the air whose loss of water indicates the evaporating power of the weather
items.s: rainfall erosivity factor: an index of the combined effect of rainfall amount and intensity on soil loss. The other options describe waterlogging, bund, evaporation pan.

items.q: outlet may be defined as
o: a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the gradient of the land increases
a value showing how readily a particular soil is lost under a standard set of conditions
the steep face between one terrace bench and the next
the point at which a drain discharges its water into a natural stream or channel
items.s: outlet: the point at which a drain discharges its water into a natural stream or channel. The other options describe soil erodibility factor, riser, slope steepness factor.

items.q: The statement “the depth of water that a drainage system is designed to remove in a stated time” describes which of the following?
o: mole drain
water table
subsurface drainage
drainage coefficient
items.s: drainage coefficient is the depth of water that a drainage system is designed to remove in a stated time.

items.q: rill erosion may be defined as
o: the moisture left in a soil after free drainage has ceased following thorough wetting
the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow
the greatest rate of flow reached at a point during or after a storm
the rapid movement of water down cracks, worm holes and root channels
items.s: rill erosion: the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow. The other options describe field capacity, preferential flow, peak discharge.

items.q: All of the following belong to Infiltration and permeability EXCEPT
o: permeability
infiltration rate
sediment delivery ratio
infiltration
items.s: Every other option belongs to Infiltration and permeability. “sediment delivery ratio” belongs to Soil erosion processes, not Infiltration and permeability.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines support practice factor.
o: the depth of soil through which the roots of a crop draw their water
a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss where conservation works are in place
the shade of a soil used as an indicator of drainage, organic matter and mineral content
the state in which every pore in the soil is filled with water
items.s: support practice factor: a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss where conservation works are in place. The other options describe soil colour, saturation, root zone depth.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines sediment yield.
o: the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water
a plot of the rate of flow at a point against time
the formation of a thin hard skin at the soil surface that resists the entry of water
the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period
items.s: sediment yield: the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period. The other options describe crusting, hydrograph, terrace channel.

items.q: Which term is described by “the mass of water held in a soil expressed as a percentage of the oven dry mass of that soil”?
o: gravimetric moisture content
moisture deficit
permanent wilting point
saturation
items.s: gravimetric moisture content is the mass of water held in a soil expressed as a percentage of the oven dry mass of that soil.

items.q: The statement “a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the gradient of the land increases” describes which of the following?
o: soil erodibility factor
support practice factor
slope steepness factor
slope length factor
items.s: slope steepness factor is a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the gradient of the land increases.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines hydraulic conductivity.
o: the constant that links the flow velocity of water in a soil to the driving head gradient
a cluster of soil particles held together by clay, organic matter or root action
the removal of a thin fairly uniform layer of soil over a whole slope
an index of the combined effect of rainfall amount and intensity on soil loss
items.s: hydraulic conductivity: the constant that links the flow velocity of water in a soil to the driving head gradient. The other options describe rainfall erosivity factor, sheet erosion, aggregate.

items.q: Which of the following best describes land grading?
o: the quantity of soil that must be moved to bring a field to its planned level
the reshaping of a field surface to a planned slope by cutting and filling
the susceptibility of a soil to being detached and carried away by erosive agents
an index of the combined effect of rainfall amount and intensity on soil loss
items.s: land grading: the reshaping of a field surface to a planned slope by cutting and filling. The other options describe erodibility, rainfall erosivity factor, earthwork volume.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines soil texture.
o: the collection and storage of runoff from a prepared surface for later use
a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss where conservation works are in place
the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay in a soil mass
the length of channel boundary in contact with flowing water
items.s: soil texture: the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay in a soil mass. The other options describe water harvesting, support practice factor, wetted perimeter.

items.q: Which term is described by “a low earth embankment thrown up to hold back water or soil”?
o: terrace
earthwork volume
cut and fill
bund
items.s: bund is a low earth embankment thrown up to hold back water or soil.

items.q: Which term is described by “a small excavated or embanked reservoir that stores runoff for later use”?
o: farm pond
hydraulic radius
Manning coefficient
evaporation pan
items.s: farm pond is a small excavated or embanked reservoir that stores runoff for later use.

items.q: Which of the following best describes waterlogging?
o: the area of land from which all surface water drains to a single point
the part of rainfall that flows over the ground surface instead of entering the soil
the cutting of a hillside into a series of level steps
the condition in which the pore space of the root zone stays filled with water
items.s: waterlogging: the condition in which the pore space of the root zone stays filled with water. The other options describe runoff, bench terracing, catchment.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines base flow.
o: the part of stream flow that comes from ground water rather than direct storm runoff
the detachment and scattering of soil particles by the impact of raindrops
the slow movement of stored water into or through the soil of a pond or channel
a small barrier across a gully that slows the flow and traps sediment
items.s: base flow: the part of stream flow that comes from ground water rather than direct storm runoff. The other options describe seepage, check dam, splash erosion.

items.q: soil loss equation may be defined as
o: the product of climate, soil, slope, cover and practice factors used to estimate long term average erosion
the lifting, sorting and carrying away of dry loose soil by moving air
the average number of years between storms that equal or exceed a stated size
the entry of water into the soil surface from rain or applied water
items.s: soil loss equation: the product of climate, soil, slope, cover and practice factors used to estimate long term average erosion. The other options describe return period, wind erosion, infiltration.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines water table?
o: the upper surface of the zone in which the soil pores are full of water
the removal of surplus water from the soil so that crops can grow
the cutting of a hillside into a series of level steps
the ease with which water moves through a soil under a pressure difference
items.s: water table: the upper surface of the zone in which the soil pores are full of water. The other options describe bench terracing, land drainage, permeability.

items.q: Which term is described by “the vertical arrangement of distinct layers seen in a cut through the soil”?
o: hardpan
soil profile
particle density
aggregate
items.s: soil profile is the vertical arrangement of distinct layers seen in a cut through the soil.

items.q: catchment may be defined as
o: tillage that leaves crop residue on the surface to shield the soil
a levelled or gently sloping bench cut into a hillside for cultivation
the depth of soil through which the roots of a crop draw their water
the area of land from which all surface water drains to a single point
items.s: catchment: the area of land from which all surface water drains to a single point. The other options describe root zone depth, conservation tillage, terrace.

items.q: The statement “the distance measured along the ground between successive conservation ridges” describes which of the following?
o: contour ploughing
horizontal spacing
vertical interval
contour bund
items.s: horizontal spacing is the distance measured along the ground between successive conservation ridges.

items.q: The statement “the cross sectional area of a channel divided by its wetted perimeter” describes which of the following?
o: shelterbelt
Manning coefficient
hydraulic radius
windbreak porosity
items.s: hydraulic radius is the cross sectional area of a channel divided by its wetted perimeter.

items.q: Which term is described by “the volume of water held in a soil expressed as a fraction of the total soil volume”?
o: permanent wilting point
available water
volumetric moisture content
gravimetric moisture content
items.s: volumetric moisture content is the volume of water held in a soil expressed as a fraction of the total soil volume.

items.q: Which term is described by “the condition in which the pore space of the root zone stays filled with water”?
o: hydraulic conductivity
Darcy law
waterlogging
infiltration
items.s: waterlogging is the condition in which the pore space of the root zone stays filled with water.

items.q: Which of the following best describes terrace?
o: an earth ridge built along the contour to hold water and trap soil
a levelled or gently sloping bench cut into a hillside for cultivation
a value showing how readily a particular soil is lost under a standard set of conditions
the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period
items.s: terrace: a levelled or gently sloping bench cut into a hillside for cultivation. The other options describe contour bund, soil erodibility factor, sediment yield.

items.q: soil texture may be defined as
o: a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the length of uninterrupted slope increases
a line drawn on the ground joining points of equal elevation
ploughing along the contour so that each furrow checks the downslope movement of water
the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay in a soil mass
items.s: soil texture: the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay in a soil mass. The other options describe contour line, contour ploughing, slope length factor.

items.q: Which term is described by “the share of the total soil volume that is occupied by air and water”?
o: aggregate
soil profile
hardpan
porosity
items.s: porosity is the share of the total soil volume that is occupied by air and water.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines rill erosion?
o: a plot of the rate of flow at a point against time
the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow
the height left between the design water level and the top of an embankment
the part of rainfall that flows over the ground surface instead of entering the soil
items.s: rill erosion: the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow. The other options describe runoff, freeboard, hydrograph.

items.q: The solid particles in a soil sample have a mass of 252 g and occupy a volume of 60 cm3. Calculate the particle density in g/cm3.
items.s: Particle density = mass of solids/volume of solids = 252/60 = 4.2 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil has a gravimetric moisture content of 18 percent and a bulk density of 1.4 g/cm3. Taking the density of water as 1 g/cm3, calculate the volumetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Volumetric moisture = gravimetric moisture x bulk density = 18 x 1.4 = 25.2 percent.

items.q: A soil to a depth of 90 cm has a volumetric moisture content of 25 percent. Calculate the depth of water stored in the soil in mm.
items.s: Depth of water = volumetric moisture x depth = 0.25 x 90 cm = 22.5 cm = 225 mm.

items.q: Water enters a soil at a steady rate of 30 mm/h over an area of 4 hectares for 2 hours. Calculate the volume of water that infiltrates in m3.
items.s: Depth entering = 30 x 2 = 60 mm, so volume = 0.06 m x 40000 m2 = 2400 m3.

items.q: Soil loss from a catchment of 5 hectares averages 20 tonnes per hectare per year and the sediment delivery ratio is 0.3. Calculate the sediment yield at the outlet in tonnes per year.
items.s: Sediment yield = soil loss x area x delivery ratio = 20 x 5 x 0.3 = 30 tonnes per year.

items.q: A storm of 65 mm falls with an energy of 22 joules per square metre per millimetre of rain. Calculate the total kinetic energy of the storm in joules per square metre.
items.s: Storm energy = rainfall x energy per millimetre = 65 x 22 = 1430 joules per square metre.

items.q: A field loses 48 tonnes of soil per hectare per year while the soil loss tolerance for that soil is 12 tonnes per hectare per year. Calculate the ratio of actual loss to the tolerance.
items.s: Ratio = actual loss/tolerance = 48/12 = 4.

items.q: A catchment of 5 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.2. Calculate the runoff volume in m3 produced by a rainfall of 45 mm.
items.s: Runoff volume = coefficient x rainfall depth x area = 0.2 x 0.045 m x 50000 m2 = 450 m3.

items.q: A storm of a stated size has a probability of 25 percent of being equalled or exceeded in any one year. Calculate its return period in years.
items.s: Return period = 100/probability = 100/25 = 4 years.

items.q: A conservation guide sets the vertical interval between contour bunds at 1.8 m for every 10 percent of land slope. For a field with a slope of 9 percent, calculate the vertical interval in m.
items.s: Vertical interval = 1.8 x 9/10 = 1.62 m.

items.q: A slope 150 m long is to be protected by contour bunds spaced 25 m apart horizontally, with a bund at the top of the slope. Calculate the number of bunds needed.
items.s: Intervals = length/spacing = 150/25 = 6, so the number of bunds including the top one is 6 + 1 = 7.

items.q: A field of 5 hectares is to be levelled by cutting an average depth of 0.18 m over the whole area. Calculate the volume of earth to be moved in m3.
items.s: Volume = area x depth = 50000 m2 x 0.18 m = 9000 m3.

items.q: A field drain falls 1 m over a length of 250 m. Calculate its gradient as a decimal fraction.
items.s: Gradient = fall/length = 1/250 = 0.004, which is 0.4 percent.

items.q: A drainage outlet discharges 45 litres per second for 12 hours. Calculate the total volume removed in m3.
items.s: Volume = discharge x time = 0.045 m3/s x 43200 s = 1944 m3.

items.q: A trapezoidal waterway carries water 0.3 m deep at a mean velocity of 0.8 m/s, its mean top width being 2.5 m. Calculate the discharge in m3/s.
items.s: Discharge = mean area x velocity = 2.5 x 0.3 x 0.8 = 0.6 m3/s.

items.q: A farm pond has a water surface area of 0.2 hectares and an average water depth of 2 m. Calculate its storage volume in m3.
items.s: Volume = surface area x depth = 2000 m2 x 2 m = 4000 m3.

items.q: A soil core of volume 250 cm3 has an oven dry mass of 314 g. Calculate the bulk density in g/cm3.
items.s: Bulk density = oven dry mass/volume = 314/250 = 1.26 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.25 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.6 g/cm3. Calculate its void ratio.
items.s: Void ratio = particle density/bulk density - 1 = 2.6/1.25 - 1 = 1.08.

items.q: A soil sample has a total volume of 300 cm3 and a porosity of 38 percent. Calculate the volume of pore space in cm3.
items.s: Pore volume = total volume x porosity/100 = 300 x 38/100 = 114 cm3.

items.q: A soil sample contains 39 percent sand and 29 percent silt. Calculate the clay content in percent.
items.s: Clay = 100 - sand - silt = 100 - 39 - 29 = 32 percent.

items.q: A soil sample has a field mass of 200 g and an oven dry mass of 170 g. Calculate the gravimetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Gravimetric moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (200 - 170)/170 x 100 = 17.6 percent.

items.q: A soil has a field capacity of 32 percent and a permanent wilting point of 14 percent by volume, with a root zone depth of 80 cm. Calculate the available water capacity in mm.
items.s: Available water = (field capacity - wilting point) x depth = (32 - 14)/100 x 80 cm = 144 mm.

items.q: A soil at field capacity holds 30 percent moisture by volume and now holds 20 percent, the root zone being 50 cm deep. Calculate the moisture deficit in mm.
items.s: Deficit = (field capacity - present moisture) x depth = (30 - 20)/100 x 50 cm = 50 mm.

items.q: A soil profile holds 90 mm of available water and the field area is 8 hectares. Calculate the total volume of available water stored in m3.
items.s: Volume = depth of water x area = 0.09 m x 80000 m2 = 7200 m3.

items.q: Water flows at 6 cm3 per minute through a soil column of cross section 80 cm2 and length 30 cm under a head difference of 30 cm. Calculate the hydraulic conductivity in cm/min.
items.s: By Darcy law K = Q L/(A H) = 6 x 30/(80 x 30) = 0.075 cm/min.

items.q: A soil has a hydraulic conductivity of 1 m/day. Water seeps through a cross section of 200 m2 under a head difference of 0.6 m over a flow path of 4 m. Calculate the seepage discharge in m3/day.
items.s: Darcy discharge = K A i = 1 x 200 x (0.6/4) = 30 m3/day.

items.q: A soil takes water at a constant rate of 30 mm/h. Calculate the depth of water that enters the soil in 2.5 hours.
items.s: Depth infiltrated = rate x time = 30 x 2.5 = 75 mm.

items.q: A canal bed of area 5000 m2 loses water into a soil of hydraulic conductivity 1.5 m/day. The water table lies so that the head gradient is 0.08. Calculate the seepage loss in m3/day.
items.s: Seepage = K A i = 1.5 x 5000 x 0.08 = 600 m3/day.

items.q: A field of 4 hectares loses 24 tonnes of soil over 4 years. Calculate the average annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Annual loss per hectare = mass/(area x years) = 24/(4 x 4) = 1.5 tonnes per hectare.

items.q: A gully has a triangular cross section 2.5 m wide at the top and 1 m deep, and runs for 80 m. Calculate the volume of soil removed in m3.
items.s: Cross sectional area = half x width x depth = 0.5 x 2.5 x 1 = 1.25 m2, so volume = 1.25 x 80 = 100 m3.

items.q: For a field the rainfall erosivity factor is 400, the soil erodibility factor is 0.35, the combined slope factor is 4, the cover and management factor is 0.3 and the support practice factor is 0.8. Calculate the estimated annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Soil loss = R x K x LS x C x P = 400 x 0.35 x 4 x 0.3 x 0.8 = 134.4 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: A field under clean cultivation loses 55 tonnes of soil per hectare per year. With a support practice whose factor is 0.5 the loss becomes that figure multiplied by the factor. Calculate the reduced soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Reduced loss = 55 x 0.5 = 27.5 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: The slope length factor of a field is calculated as (slope length/reference length) raised to the power 0.5, where the reference length is 22 m. For a slope length of 40 m, calculate the slope length factor.
items.s: Slope length factor = (40/22)^0.5 = 1.35.

items.q: Each tonne of crop residue left on the surface covers 25 percent of the ground. Calculate the percentage cover left by 4 tonnes of residue per hectare.
items.s: Cover = residue x cover per tonne = 4 x 25 = 100 percent.

items.q: A storm of 40 mm on a catchment of 4 hectares produced a runoff volume of 4800 m3. Calculate the runoff coefficient.
items.s: Rainfall volume = 0.04 m x 40000 m2 = 1600 m3, so runoff coefficient = 4800/1600 = 3.

items.q: A catchment of 8 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.7 and the design rainfall intensity for its time of concentration is 120 mm/h. Calculate the peak discharge by the rational method in m3/s.
items.s: Peak discharge = C x i x A/360 = 0.7 x 120 x 8/360 = 1.87 m3/s.

items.q: A storm delivers 48 mm of rain in 0.5 hours. Calculate the average rainfall intensity in mm/h.
items.s: Intensity = depth/duration = 48/0.5 = 96 mm/h.

items.q: At the outlet of a catchment the base flow is 1.2 m3/s and the direct storm runoff is 7.5 m3/s. Calculate the total stream flow in m3/s.
items.s: Total flow = base flow + direct runoff = 1.2 + 7.5 = 8.7 m3/s.

items.q: A catchment of 5 hectares produces a runoff volume of 12000 m3. Calculate the depth of runoff over the catchment in mm.
items.s: Depth = volume/area = 12000/50000 m2 = 0.24 m = 240 mm.

items.q: A runoff depth of 30 mm is produced from a catchment of 10 hectares and leaves the outlet over 4 hours. Calculate the average rate of flow in m3/s.
Ground rises 12 m over a horizontal distance of 50 m. Calculate the land slope in percent.
items.s: Slope = rise/run x 100 = 12/50 x 100 = 24 percent.

items.q: A field has a slope of 6 percent. Calculate the angle of the slope in degrees.
items.s: Slope angle = arctan(6/100) = 3.43 degrees.

items.q: Contour bunds are to be laid with a vertical interval of 3 m on land of 12 percent slope. Calculate the horizontal spacing between bunds in m.
items.s: Horizontal spacing = vertical interval/(slope/100) = 3/(12/100) = 25 m.

items.q: A contour bund has a triangular cross section 0.6 m wide at the base and 0.4 m high and is 200 m long. Calculate the volume of earth in it in m3.
items.s: Volume = half x base x height x length = 0.5 x 0.6 x 0.4 x 200 = 24 m3.

items.q: A gully 450 m long is to be treated with check dams spaced 50 m apart, with one at the head of the gully. Calculate the number of check dams required.
items.s: Intervals = gully length/spacing = 450/50 = 9, so the number of check dams including the one at the head is 9 + 1 = 10.

items.q: A terrace bench of width 3 m is to serve an area of 1 hectares. Calculate the total length of terrace in m.
items.s: Length = area/width = 10000 m2/3 m = 3333 m.

items.q: A field is graded so that it falls 0.45 m along a run of 250 m. Calculate the graded slope in percent.
items.s: Graded slope = fall/run x 100 = 0.45/250 x 100 = 0.18 percent.

items.q: A farm pond is designed to hold water to a depth of 1.8 m and must be given a freeboard of 0.2 m. Calculate the height of the embankment in m.
items.s: Embankment height = water depth + freeboard = 1.8 + 0.2 = 2 m.

items.q: A drainage system must remove 8 mm of water from 4 hectares within 24 hours. Calculate the required discharge in litres per second.
items.s: Volume = 0.008 m x 40000 m2 = 320 m3, so discharge = 320 m3/(24 x 3600 s) = 3.7 litres per second.

items.q: A field 336 m wide is to be drained by parallel field drains spaced 24 m apart, with a drain along each edge. Calculate the number of drain lines required.
items.s: Intervals = width/spacing = 336/24 = 14, so the number of lines with one on each edge is 14 + 1 = 15.

items.q: A field of 4 hectares is to be underdrained with parallel drains spaced 15 m apart. Calculate the total length of drain required in m.
items.s: Total length = area/spacing = 40000 m2/15 m = 2667 m.

items.q: A grassed waterway has a Manning coefficient of 0.04, a hydraulic radius of 0.6 m and a bed slope of 0.004. Calculate the flow velocity in m/s.
A rectangular waterway is 0.8 m wide and carries water 0.2 m deep. Calculate its hydraulic radius in m.
items.s: Area = 0.8 x 0.2 = 0.16 m2 and wetted perimeter = 0.8 + 2 x 0.2 = 1.2 m, so hydraulic radius = 0.1333 m.

items.q: A farmer needs to store 900 m3 of water from a catchment that receives 300 mm of rain a year, with a runoff efficiency of 0.7. Calculate the catchment area needed in hectares.
items.s: Yield per hectare = 0.3 m x 0.7 = 0.21 m3, so area = 900/0.21 = 0.43 hectares = 0.4286.

items.q: A shelterbelt is planted with trees 10 m tall and a spacing rule of 12 times the tree height is used. Calculate the spacing between shelterbelts in m.
items.s: Spacing = tree height x multiple = 10 x 12 = 120 m.

items.q: An evaporation pan loses 9 mm of water in a day and the pan coefficient for the station is 0.75. Calculate the estimated evaporation from a water surface in mm per day.
items.s: Evaporation = pan loss x pan coefficient = 9 x 0.75 = 6.75 mm per day.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.45 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.65 g/cm3. Calculate its porosity in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/particle density) x 100 = (1 - 1.45/2.65) x 100 = 45.3 percent.

items.q: The solid particles in a soil sample have a mass of 192 g and occupy a volume of 50 cm3. Calculate the particle density in g/cm3.
items.s: Particle density = mass of solids/volume of solids = 192/50 = 3.84 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil has a gravimetric moisture content of 18 percent and a bulk density of 1.5 g/cm3. Taking the density of water as 1 g/cm3, calculate the volumetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Volumetric moisture = gravimetric moisture x bulk density = 18 x 1.5 = 27 percent.

items.q: A soil to a depth of 40 cm has a volumetric moisture content of 28 percent. Calculate the depth of water stored in the soil in mm.
items.s: Depth of water = volumetric moisture x depth = 0.28 x 40 cm = 11.2 cm = 112 mm.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the amount by which the water present in the root zone falls short of field capacity”
o: saturation
moisture deficit
hygroscopic water
permanent wilting point
items.s: moisture deficit is the amount by which the water present in the root zone falls short of field capacity.

items.q: In this course, sheet erosion refers to
o: the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period
the removal of a thin fairly uniform layer of soil over a whole slope
the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow
the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet
items.s: sheet erosion: the removal of a thin fairly uniform layer of soil over a whole slope. The other options describe rill erosion, sediment yield, sediment delivery ratio.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Contour and conservation practice?
o: contour ploughing
contour bund
contour line
time of concentration
items.s: Every other option belongs to Contour and conservation practice. “time of concentration” belongs to Runoff and small catchment hydrology, not Contour and conservation practice.

items.q: The best definition of mulching among these is
o: an index of the combined effect of rainfall amount and intensity on soil loss
a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the gradient of the land increases
a value showing how readily a particular soil is lost under a standard set of conditions
the spreading of plant material over the soil surface to absorb raindrop energy and hold moisture
items.s: mulching: the spreading of plant material over the soil surface to absorb raindrop energy and hold moisture. The other options describe slope steepness factor, soil erodibility factor, rainfall erosivity factor.

items.q: The statement “a plot of the rate of flow at a point against time” describes which of the following?
o: rainfall intensity
hydrograph
runoff coefficient
runoff
items.s: hydrograph is a plot of the rate of flow at a point against time.

items.q: porosity is best described as
o: the vertical arrangement of distinct layers seen in a cut through the soil
the volume of voids in a soil divided by the volume of its solid particles
the share of the total soil volume that is occupied by air and water
the mass of the solid particles of a soil divided by the volume of those solids alone
items.s: porosity: the share of the total soil volume that is occupied by air and water. The other options describe particle density, soil profile, void ratio.

items.q: graded bund is best described as
o: an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet
the height difference between one conservation ridge and the next down the slope
a shallow vegetated channel that carries concentrated runoff safely down a slope
ploughing along the contour so that each furrow checks the downslope movement of water
items.s: graded bund: an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet. The other options describe contour ploughing, vertical interval, grassed waterway.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the cross sectional area of a channel divided by its wetted perimeter”
o: Manning coefficient
hydraulic radius
seepage
farm pond
items.s: hydraulic radius is the cross sectional area of a channel divided by its wetted perimeter.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the vertical arrangement of distinct layers seen in a cut through the soil”
o: soil profile
porosity
particle density
soil colour
items.s: soil profile is the vertical arrangement of distinct layers seen in a cut through the soil.

items.q: Which term is described by “the lifting, sorting and carrying away of dry loose soil by moving air”?
o: wind erosion
gully erosion
splash erosion
sediment delivery ratio
items.s: wind erosion is the lifting, sorting and carrying away of dry loose soil by moving air.

items.q: splash erosion is best described as
o: the greatest rate of erosion that a soil can suffer without losing productivity
the enlargement of rills into deep channels that cannot be crossed by farm machinery
the detachment and scattering of soil particles by the impact of raindrops
the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period
items.s: splash erosion: the detachment and scattering of soil particles by the impact of raindrops. The other options describe gully erosion, soil loss tolerance, sediment yield.

items.q: The statement “the product of climate, soil, slope, cover and practice factors used to estimate long term average erosion” describes which of the following?

items.q: A soil has a field capacity of 28 percent and a permanent wilting point of 15 percent by volume, with a root zone depth of 80 cm. Calculate the available water capacity in mm.
items.s: Available water = (field capacity - wilting point) x depth = (28 - 15)/100 x 80 cm = 104 mm.

items.q: A soil at field capacity holds 32 percent moisture by volume and now holds 22 percent, the root zone being 50 cm deep. Calculate the moisture deficit in mm.
items.s: Deficit = (field capacity - present moisture) x depth = (32 - 22)/100 x 50 cm = 50 mm.

items.q: A soil has a hydraulic conductivity of 2.5 m/day. Water seeps through a cross section of 400 m2 under a head difference of 0.5 m over a flow path of 2.5 m. Calculate the seepage discharge in m3/day.
items.s: Darcy discharge = K A i = 2.5 x 400 x (0.5/2.5) = 200 m3/day.

items.q: Each tonne of crop residue left on the surface covers 30 percent of the ground. Calculate the percentage cover left by 4 tonnes of residue per hectare.
items.s: Cover = residue x cover per tonne = 4 x 30 = 120 percent.

items.q: A storm of 50 mm on a catchment of 2 hectares produced a runoff volume of 3000 m3. Calculate the runoff coefficient.
items.s: Rainfall volume = 0.05 m x 20000 m2 = 1000 m3, so runoff coefficient = 3000/1000 = 3.

items.q: A catchment of 2 hectares produces a runoff volume of 18000 m3. Calculate the depth of runoff over the catchment in mm.
items.s: Depth = volume/area = 18000/20000 m2 = 0.9 m = 900 mm.

items.q: A runoff depth of 20 mm is produced from a catchment of 10 hectares and leaves the outlet over 6 hours. Calculate the average rate of flow in m3/s.
A field has a slope of 15 percent. Calculate the angle of the slope in degrees.
items.s: Slope angle = arctan(15/100) = 8.53 degrees.

items.q: Contour bunds are to be laid with a vertical interval of 1.5 m on land of 5 percent slope. Calculate the horizontal spacing between bunds in m.
items.s: Horizontal spacing = vertical interval/(slope/100) = 1.5/(5/100) = 30 m.

items.q: A contour bund has a triangular cross section 0.75 m wide at the base and 0.4 m high and is 150 m long. Calculate the volume of earth in it in m3.
items.s: Volume = half x base x height x length = 0.5 x 0.75 x 0.4 x 150 = 22.5 m3.

items.q: A terrace bench of width 3.5 m is to serve an area of 0.8 hectares. Calculate the total length of terrace in m.
items.s: Length = area/width = 8000 m2/3.5 m = 2286 m.

items.q: A field of 5 hectares is to be underdrained with parallel drains spaced 12 m apart. Calculate the total length of drain required in m.
items.s: Total length = area/spacing = 50000 m2/12 m = 4167 m.

items.q: A rectangular waterway is 1.2 m wide and carries water 0.5 m deep. Calculate its hydraulic radius in m.
items.s: Area = 1.2 x 0.5 = 0.6 m2 and wetted perimeter = 1.2 + 2 x 0.5 = 2.2 m, so hydraulic radius = 0.2727 m.

items.q: A soil core of volume 200 cm3 has an oven dry mass of 442 g. Calculate the bulk density in g/cm3.
items.s: Bulk density = oven dry mass/volume = 442/200 = 2.21 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.2 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.6 g/cm3. Calculate its porosity in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/particle density) x 100 = (1 - 1.2/2.6) x 100 = 53.8 percent.

items.q: The solid particles in a soil sample have a mass of 190 g and occupy a volume of 90 cm3. Calculate the particle density in g/cm3.
items.s: Particle density = mass of solids/volume of solids = 190/90 = 2.11 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil sample has a total volume of 250 cm3 and a porosity of 55 percent. Calculate the volume of pore space in cm3.
items.s: Pore volume = total volume x porosity/100 = 250 x 55/100 = 137.5 cm3.

items.q: A soil sample contains 30 percent sand and 24 percent silt. Calculate the clay content in percent.
items.s: Clay = 100 - sand - silt = 100 - 30 - 24 = 46 percent.

items.q: A soil sample has a field mass of 221 g and an oven dry mass of 91 g. Calculate the gravimetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Gravimetric moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (221 - 91)/91 x 100 = 142.9 percent.

items.q: A soil has a gravimetric moisture content of 18 percent and a bulk density of 1.35 g/cm3. Taking the density of water as 1 g/cm3, calculate the volumetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Volumetric moisture = gravimetric moisture x bulk density = 18 x 1.35 = 24.3 percent.

items.q: A soil to a depth of 75 cm has a volumetric moisture content of 20 percent. Calculate the depth of water stored in the soil in mm.
items.s: Depth of water = volumetric moisture x depth = 0.2 x 75 cm = 15 cm = 150 mm.

items.q: A soil profile holds 75 mm of available water and the field area is 6 hectares. Calculate the total volume of available water stored in m3.
items.s: Volume = depth of water x area = 0.075 m x 60000 m2 = 4500 m3.

items.q: Water enters a soil at a steady rate of 20 mm/h over an area of 4 hectares for 2 hours. Calculate the volume of water that infiltrates in m3.
items.s: Depth entering = 20 x 2 = 40 mm, so volume = 0.04 m x 40000 m2 = 1600 m3.

items.q: Water flows at 6 cm3 per minute through a soil column of cross section 50 cm2 and length 30 cm under a head difference of 10 cm. Calculate the hydraulic conductivity in cm/min.
items.s: By Darcy law K = Q L/(A H) = 6 x 30/(50 x 10) = 0.36 cm/min.

items.q: A soil takes water at a constant rate of 36 mm/h. Calculate the depth of water that enters the soil in 1.5 hours.
items.s: Depth infiltrated = rate x time = 36 x 1.5 = 54 mm.

items.q: A canal bed of area 1000 m2 loses water into a soil of hydraulic conductivity 2 m/day. The water table lies so that the head gradient is 0.03. Calculate the seepage loss in m3/day.
items.s: Seepage = K A i = 2 x 1000 x 0.03 = 60 m3/day.

items.q: A field of 4 hectares loses 12 tonnes of soil over 2 years. Calculate the average annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Annual loss per hectare = mass/(area x years) = 12/(4 x 2) = 1.5 tonnes per hectare.

items.q: Soil loss from a catchment of 5 hectares averages 20 tonnes per hectare per year and the sediment delivery ratio is 0.2. Calculate the sediment yield at the outlet in tonnes per year.
items.s: Sediment yield = soil loss x area x delivery ratio = 20 x 5 x 0.2 = 20 tonnes per year.

items.q: A storm of 55 mm falls with an energy of 25 joules per square metre per millimetre of rain. Calculate the total kinetic energy of the storm in joules per square metre.
items.s: Storm energy = rainfall x energy per millimetre = 55 x 25 = 1375 joules per square metre.

items.q: For a field the rainfall erosivity factor is 400, the soil erodibility factor is 0.2, the combined slope factor is 3, the cover and management factor is 0.2 and the support practice factor is 0.8. Calculate the estimated annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Soil loss = R x K x LS x C x P = 400 x 0.2 x 3 x 0.2 x 0.8 = 38.4 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: A field under clean cultivation loses 55 tonnes of soil per hectare per year. With a support practice whose factor is 0.8 the loss becomes that figure multiplied by the factor. Calculate the reduced soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Reduced loss = 55 x 0.8 = 44 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: The slope length factor of a field is calculated as (slope length/reference length) raised to the power 0.5, where the reference length is 25 m. For a slope length of 20 m, calculate the slope length factor.
items.s: Slope length factor = (20/25)^0.5 = 0.894.

items.q: A field loses 25 tonnes of soil per hectare per year while the soil loss tolerance for that soil is 8 tonnes per hectare per year. Calculate the ratio of actual loss to the tolerance.
items.s: Ratio = actual loss/tolerance = 25/8 = 3.12.

items.q: A catchment of 5 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.5. Calculate the runoff volume in m3 produced by a rainfall of 85 mm.
items.s: Runoff volume = coefficient x rainfall depth x area = 0.5 x 0.085 m x 50000 m2 = 2125 m3.

items.q: A catchment of 20 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.5 and the design rainfall intensity for its time of concentration is 75 mm/h. Calculate the peak discharge by the rational method in m3/s.
items.s: Peak discharge = C x i x A/360 = 0.5 x 75 x 20/360 = 2.08 m3/s.

items.q: At the outlet of a catchment the base flow is 0.4 m3/s and the direct storm runoff is 2 m3/s. Calculate the total stream flow in m3/s.
items.s: Total flow = base flow + direct runoff = 0.4 + 2 = 2.4 m3/s.

items.q: Ground rises 4.5 m over a horizontal distance of 50 m. Calculate the land slope in percent.
items.s: Slope = rise/run x 100 = 4.5/50 x 100 = 9 percent.

items.q: A conservation guide sets the vertical interval between contour bunds at 1.8 m for every 10 percent of land slope. For a field with a slope of 12 percent, calculate the vertical interval in m.
items.s: Vertical interval = 1.8 x 12/10 = 2.16 m.

items.q: A slope 75 m long is to be protected by contour bunds spaced 15 m apart horizontally, with a bund at the top of the slope. Calculate the number of bunds needed.
items.s: Intervals = length/spacing = 75/15 = 5, so the number of bunds including the top one is 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: A gully 480 m long is to be treated with check dams spaced 40 m apart, with one at the head of the gully. Calculate the number of check dams required.
items.s: Intervals = gully length/spacing = 480/40 = 12, so the number of check dams including the one at the head is 12 + 1 = 13.

items.q: A field of 1 hectares is to be levelled by cutting an average depth of 0.15 m over the whole area. Calculate the volume of earth to be moved in m3.
items.s: Volume = area x depth = 10000 m2 x 0.15 m = 1500 m3.

items.q: A field is graded so that it falls 0.6 m along a run of 150 m. Calculate the graded slope in percent.
items.s: Graded slope = fall/run x 100 = 0.6/150 x 100 = 0.4 percent.

items.q: A farm pond is designed to hold water to a depth of 2 m and must be given a freeboard of 0.3 m. Calculate the height of the embankment in m.
items.s: Embankment height = water depth + freeboard = 2 + 0.3 = 2.3 m.

items.q: A drainage system must remove 20 mm of water from 12 hectares within 48 hours. Calculate the required discharge in litres per second.
items.s: Volume = 0.02 m x 120000 m2 = 2400 m3, so discharge = 2400 m3/(48 x 3600 s) = 13.89 litres per second.

items.q: A field drain falls 1.5 m over a length of 300 m. Calculate its gradient as a decimal fraction.
items.s: Gradient = fall/length = 1.5/300 = 0.005, which is 0.5 percent.

items.q: A field 140 m wide is to be drained by parallel field drains spaced 20 m apart, with a drain along each edge. Calculate the number of drain lines required.
items.s: Intervals = width/spacing = 140/20 = 7, so the number of lines with one on each edge is 7 + 1 = 8.

items.q: A drainage outlet discharges 30 litres per second for 12 hours. Calculate the total volume removed in m3.
items.s: Volume = discharge x time = 0.03 m3/s x 43200 s = 1296 m3.

items.q: A grassed waterway has a Manning coefficient of 0.035, a hydraulic radius of 0.4 m and a bed slope of 0.003. Calculate the flow velocity in m/s.
A trapezoidal waterway carries water 0.25 m deep at a mean velocity of 1.5 m/s, its mean top width being 2.5 m. Calculate the discharge in m3/s.
items.s: Discharge = mean area x velocity = 2.5 x 0.25 x 1.5 = 0.938 m3/s.

items.q: A farm pond has a water surface area of 0.4 hectares and an average water depth of 1.5 m. Calculate its storage volume in m3.
items.s: Volume = surface area x depth = 4000 m2 x 1.5 m = 6000 m3.

items.q: A shelterbelt is planted with trees 8 m tall and a spacing rule of 10 times the tree height is used. Calculate the spacing between shelterbelts in m.
items.s: Spacing = tree height x multiple = 8 x 10 = 80 m.

items.q: An evaporation pan loses 7.5 mm of water in a day and the pan coefficient for the station is 0.75. Calculate the estimated evaporation from a water surface in mm per day.
items.s: Evaporation = pan loss x pan coefficient = 7.5 x 0.75 = 5.62 mm per day.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.35 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.6 g/cm3. Calculate its void ratio.
items.s: Void ratio = particle density/bulk density - 1 = 2.6/1.35 - 1 = 0.926.

items.q: A soil has a field capacity of 30 percent and a permanent wilting point of 12 percent by volume, with a root zone depth of 50 cm. Calculate the available water capacity in mm.
items.s: Available water = (field capacity - wilting point) x depth = (30 - 12)/100 x 50 cm = 90 mm.

items.q: A soil at field capacity holds 30 percent moisture by volume and now holds 22 percent, the root zone being 40 cm deep. Calculate the moisture deficit in mm.
items.s: Deficit = (field capacity - present moisture) x depth = (30 - 22)/100 x 40 cm = 32 mm.

items.q: A soil has a hydraulic conductivity of 1 m/day. Water seeps through a cross section of 800 m2 under a head difference of 0.4 m over a flow path of 2 m. Calculate the seepage discharge in m3/day.
items.s: Darcy discharge = K A i = 1 x 800 x (0.4/2) = 160 m3/day.

items.q: A gully has a triangular cross section 1.5 m wide at the top and 1.2 m deep, and runs for 80 m. Calculate the volume of soil removed in m3.
items.s: Cross sectional area = half x width x depth = 0.5 x 1.5 x 1.2 = 0.9 m2, so volume = 0.9 x 80 = 72 m3.

items.q: Each tonne of crop residue left on the surface covers 35 percent of the ground. Calculate the percentage cover left by 2 tonnes of residue per hectare.
items.s: Cover = residue x cover per tonne = 2 x 35 = 70 percent.

items.q: A storm of 40 mm on a catchment of 3 hectares produced a runoff volume of 4800 m3. Calculate the runoff coefficient.
items.s: Rainfall volume = 0.04 m x 30000 m2 = 1200 m3, so runoff coefficient = 4800/1200 = 4.

items.q: A catchment of 8 hectares produces a runoff volume of 9000 m3. Calculate the depth of runoff over the catchment in mm.
items.s: Depth = volume/area = 9000/80000 m2 = 0.113 m = 112.5 mm.
