o: the downward movement of water through the soil body below the surface layer
the rapid movement of water down cracks, worm holes and root channels
the entry of water into the soil surface from rain or applied water
the ease with which water moves through a soil under a pressure difference
items.s: infiltration: the entry of water into the soil surface from rain or applied water. The other options describe permeability, percolation, preferential flow.

items.q: Which term is described by “the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay in a soil mass”?
o: soil texture
particle density
bulk density
void ratio
items.s: soil texture is the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay in a soil mass.

items.q: Which of the following best describes shelterbelt?
o: an open vessel of water exposed to the air whose loss of water indicates the evaporating power of the weather
the collection and storage of runoff from a prepared surface for later use
a row or belt of trees planted to slow the wind over nearby land
the cross sectional area of a channel divided by its wetted perimeter
items.s: shelterbelt: a row or belt of trees planted to slow the wind over nearby land. The other options describe hydraulic radius, water harvesting, evaporation pan.

items.q: sediment delivery ratio is best described as
o: the lifting, sorting and carrying away of dry loose soil by moving air
the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow
the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period
the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet
items.s: sediment delivery ratio: the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet. The other options describe wind erosion, rill erosion, sediment yield.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines hydraulic radius?
o: a row or belt of trees planted to slow the wind over nearby land
the cross sectional area of a channel divided by its wetted perimeter
a roughness value that expresses the resistance a channel bed and sides offer to flow
a small excavated or embanked reservoir that stores runoff for later use
items.s: hydraulic radius: the cross sectional area of a channel divided by its wetted perimeter. The other options describe shelterbelt, Manning coefficient, farm pond.

items.q: Water flows at 6 cm3 per minute through a soil column of cross section 120 cm2 and length 40 cm under a head difference of 25 cm. Calculate the hydraulic conductivity in cm/min.
items.s: By Darcy law K = Q L/(A H) = 6 x 40/(120 x 25) = 0.08 cm/min.

items.q: A canal bed of area 1000 m2 loses water into a soil of hydraulic conductivity 0.8 m/day. The water table lies so that the head gradient is 0.03. Calculate the seepage loss in m3/day.
items.s: Seepage = K A i = 0.8 x 1000 x 0.03 = 24 m3/day.

items.q: For a field the rainfall erosivity factor is 400, the soil erodibility factor is 0.2, the combined slope factor is 2.5, the cover and management factor is 0.2 and the support practice factor is 0.5. Calculate the estimated annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Soil loss = R x K x LS x C x P = 400 x 0.2 x 2.5 x 0.2 x 0.5 = 20 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: The slope length factor of a field is calculated as (slope length/reference length) raised to the power 0.5, where the reference length is 22 m. For a slope length of 60 m, calculate the slope length factor.
items.s: Slope length factor = (60/22)^0.5 = 1.65.

items.q: A catchment of 10 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.7 and the design rainfall intensity for its time of concentration is 90 mm/h. Calculate the peak discharge by the rational method in m3/s.
items.s: Peak discharge = C x i x A/360 = 0.7 x 90 x 10/360 = 1.75 m3/s.

items.q: A drainage system must remove 10 mm of water from 6 hectares within 48 hours. Calculate the required discharge in litres per second.
items.s: Volume = 0.01 m x 60000 m2 = 600 m3, so discharge = 600 m3/(48 x 3600 s) = 3.47 litres per second.

items.q: A grassed waterway has a Manning coefficient of 0.04, a hydraulic radius of 0.4 m and a bed slope of 0.005. Calculate the flow velocity in m/s.
A farmer needs to store 900 m3 of water from a catchment that receives 250 mm of rain a year, with a runoff efficiency of 0.7. Calculate the catchment area needed in hectares.
items.s: Yield per hectare = 0.25 m x 0.7 = 0.175 m3, so area = 900/0.175 = 0.51 hectares = 0.5143.

items.q: A soil core of volume 300 cm3 has an oven dry mass of 272 g. Calculate the bulk density in g/cm3.
items.s: Bulk density = oven dry mass/volume = 272/300 = 0.91 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.55 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.65 g/cm3. Calculate its porosity in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/particle density) x 100 = (1 - 1.55/2.65) x 100 = 41.5 percent.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.25 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.65 g/cm3. Calculate its void ratio.
items.s: Void ratio = particle density/bulk density - 1 = 2.65/1.25 - 1 = 1.12.

items.q: The solid particles in a soil sample have a mass of 162 g and occupy a volume of 90 cm3. Calculate the particle density in g/cm3.
items.s: Particle density = mass of solids/volume of solids = 162/90 = 1.8 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil sample has a total volume of 200 cm3 and a porosity of 42 percent. Calculate the volume of pore space in cm3.
items.s: Pore volume = total volume x porosity/100 = 200 x 42/100 = 84 cm3.

items.q: A soil sample contains 49 percent sand and 32 percent silt. Calculate the clay content in percent.
items.s: Clay = 100 - sand - silt = 100 - 49 - 32 = 19 percent.

items.q: A soil sample has a field mass of 251 g and an oven dry mass of 114 g. Calculate the gravimetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Gravimetric moisture = (wet mass - dry mass)/dry mass x 100 = (251 - 114)/114 x 100 = 120.2 percent.

items.q: A soil has a gravimetric moisture content of 12 percent and a bulk density of 1.2 g/cm3. Taking the density of water as 1 g/cm3, calculate the volumetric moisture content in percent.
items.s: Volumetric moisture = gravimetric moisture x bulk density = 12 x 1.2 = 14.4 percent.

items.q: A soil to a depth of 75 cm has a volumetric moisture content of 25 percent. Calculate the depth of water stored in the soil in mm.
items.s: Depth of water = volumetric moisture x depth = 0.25 x 75 cm = 18.75 cm = 187.5 mm.

items.q: A soil has a field capacity of 32 percent and a permanent wilting point of 12 percent by volume, with a root zone depth of 50 cm. Calculate the available water capacity in mm.
items.s: Available water = (field capacity - wilting point) x depth = (32 - 12)/100 x 50 cm = 100 mm.

items.q: A soil at field capacity holds 28 percent moisture by volume and now holds 20 percent, the root zone being 50 cm deep. Calculate the moisture deficit in mm.
items.s: Deficit = (field capacity - present moisture) x depth = (28 - 20)/100 x 50 cm = 40 mm.

items.q: Water enters a soil at a steady rate of 10 mm/h over an area of 2 hectares for 2 hours. Calculate the volume of water that infiltrates in m3.
items.s: Depth entering = 10 x 2 = 20 mm, so volume = 0.02 m x 20000 m2 = 400 m3.

items.q: A soil has a hydraulic conductivity of 0.5 m/day. Water seeps through a cross section of 200 m2 under a head difference of 0.6 m over a flow path of 2.5 m. Calculate the seepage discharge in m3/day.
items.s: Darcy discharge = K A i = 0.5 x 200 x (0.6/2.5) = 24 m3/day.

items.q: A field of 4 hectares loses 45 tonnes of soil over 5 years. Calculate the average annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Annual loss per hectare = mass/(area x years) = 45/(4 x 5) = 2.25 tonnes per hectare.

items.q: Soil loss from a catchment of 12 hectares averages 20 tonnes per hectare per year and the sediment delivery ratio is 0.4. Calculate the sediment yield at the outlet in tonnes per year.
items.s: Sediment yield = soil loss x area x delivery ratio = 20 x 12 x 0.4 = 96 tonnes per year.

items.q: A storm of 40 mm falls with an energy of 28 joules per square metre per millimetre of rain. Calculate the total kinetic energy of the storm in joules per square metre.
items.s: Storm energy = rainfall x energy per millimetre = 40 x 28 = 1120 joules per square metre.

items.q: A gully has a triangular cross section 2 m wide at the top and 0.8 m deep, and runs for 100 m. Calculate the volume of soil removed in m3.
items.s: Cross sectional area = half x width x depth = 0.5 x 2 x 0.8 = 0.8 m2, so volume = 0.8 x 100 = 80 m3.

items.q: A field under clean cultivation loses 40 tonnes of soil per hectare per year. With a support practice whose factor is 0.5 the loss becomes that figure multiplied by the factor. Calculate the reduced soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Reduced loss = 40 x 0.5 = 20 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: A field loses 8 tonnes of soil per hectare per year while the soil loss tolerance for that soil is 8 tonnes per hectare per year. Calculate the ratio of actual loss to the tolerance.
items.s: Ratio = actual loss/tolerance = 8/8 = 1.

items.q: Each tonne of crop residue left on the surface covers 30 percent of the ground. Calculate the percentage cover left by 1.5 tonnes of residue per hectare.
items.s: Cover = residue x cover per tonne = 1.5 x 30 = 45 percent.

items.q: A storm of 50 mm on a catchment of 8 hectares produced a runoff volume of 9000 m3. Calculate the runoff coefficient.
items.s: Rainfall volume = 0.05 m x 80000 m2 = 4000 m3, so runoff coefficient = 9000/4000 = 2.25.

items.q: A catchment of 12 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.35. Calculate the runoff volume in m3 produced by a rainfall of 45 mm.
items.s: Runoff volume = coefficient x rainfall depth x area = 0.35 x 0.045 m x 120000 m2 = 1890 m3.

items.q: A storm of a stated size has a probability of 4 percent of being equalled or exceeded in any one year. Calculate its return period in years.
items.s: Return period = 100/probability = 100/4 = 25 years.

items.q: At the outlet of a catchment the base flow is 0.8 m3/s and the direct storm runoff is 5 m3/s. Calculate the total stream flow in m3/s.
items.s: Total flow = base flow + direct runoff = 0.8 + 5 = 5.8 m3/s.

items.q: A catchment of 3 hectares produces a runoff volume of 4000 m3. Calculate the depth of runoff over the catchment in mm.
items.s: Depth = volume/area = 4000/30000 m2 = 0.133 m = 133.3 mm.

items.q: A runoff depth of 20 mm is produced from a catchment of 20 hectares and leaves the outlet over 4 hours. Calculate the average rate of flow in m3/s.
Ground rises 9 m over a horizontal distance of 75 m. Calculate the land slope in percent.
items.s: Slope = rise/run x 100 = 9/75 x 100 = 12 percent.

items.q: A conservation guide sets the vertical interval between contour bunds at 1.8 m for every 10 percent of land slope. For a field with a slope of 18 percent, calculate the vertical interval in m.
items.s: Vertical interval = 1.8 x 18/10 = 3.24 m.

items.q: Contour bunds are to be laid with a vertical interval of 2.4 m on land of 12 percent slope. Calculate the horizontal spacing between bunds in m.
items.s: Horizontal spacing = vertical interval/(slope/100) = 2.4/(12/100) = 20 m.

items.q: A field of 1 hectares is to be levelled by cutting an average depth of 0.12 m over the whole area. Calculate the volume of earth to be moved in m3.
items.s: Volume = area x depth = 10000 m2 x 0.12 m = 1200 m3.

items.q: A terrace bench of width 3.5 m is to serve an area of 0.5 hectares. Calculate the total length of terrace in m.
items.s: Length = area/width = 5000 m2/3.5 m = 1429 m.

items.q: A field is graded so that it falls 1.2 m along a run of 250 m. Calculate the graded slope in percent.
items.s: Graded slope = fall/run x 100 = 1.2/250 x 100 = 0.48 percent.

items.q: A farm pond is designed to hold water to a depth of 1.8 m and must be given a freeboard of 0.25 m. Calculate the height of the embankment in m.
items.s: Embankment height = water depth + freeboard = 1.8 + 0.25 = 2.05 m.

items.q: A field drain falls 0.4 m over a length of 200 m. Calculate its gradient as a decimal fraction.
items.s: Gradient = fall/length = 0.4/200 = 0.002, which is 0.2 percent.

items.q: A field 96 m wide is to be drained by parallel field drains spaced 12 m apart, with a drain along each edge. Calculate the number of drain lines required.
items.s: Intervals = width/spacing = 96/12 = 8, so the number of lines with one on each edge is 8 + 1 = 9.

items.q: A field of 4 hectares is to be underdrained with parallel drains spaced 20 m apart. Calculate the total length of drain required in m.
items.s: Total length = area/spacing = 40000 m2/20 m = 2000 m.

items.q: A drainage outlet discharges 18 litres per second for 6 hours. Calculate the total volume removed in m3.
items.s: Volume = discharge x time = 0.018 m3/s x 21600 s = 389 m3.

items.q: A trapezoidal waterway carries water 0.4 m deep at a mean velocity of 1.2 m/s, its mean top width being 2 m. Calculate the discharge in m3/s.
items.s: Discharge = mean area x velocity = 2 x 0.4 x 1.2 = 0.96 m3/s.

items.q: A farm pond has a water surface area of 0.2 hectares and an average water depth of 2.5 m. Calculate its storage volume in m3.
items.s: Volume = surface area x depth = 2000 m2 x 2.5 m = 5000 m3.

items.q: A shelterbelt is planted with trees 8 m tall and a spacing rule of 15 times the tree height is used. Calculate the spacing between shelterbelts in m.
items.s: Spacing = tree height x multiple = 8 x 15 = 120 m.

items.q: An evaporation pan loses 5 mm of water in a day and the pan coefficient for the station is 0.75. Calculate the estimated evaporation from a water surface in mm per day.
items.s: Evaporation = pan loss x pan coefficient = 5 x 0.75 = 3.75 mm per day.

items.q: A soil profile holds 40 mm of available water and the field area is 2 hectares. Calculate the total volume of available water stored in m3.
items.s: Volume = depth of water x area = 0.04 m x 20000 m2 = 800 m3.

items.q: Water flows at 4 cm3 per minute through a soil column of cross section 120 cm2 and length 30 cm under a head difference of 10 cm. Calculate the hydraulic conductivity in cm/min.
items.s: By Darcy law K = Q L/(A H) = 4 x 30/(120 x 10) = 0.1 cm/min.

items.q: A canal bed of area 2000 m2 loses water into a soil of hydraulic conductivity 1.5 m/day. The water table lies so that the head gradient is 0.03. Calculate the seepage loss in m3/day.
items.s: Seepage = K A i = 1.5 x 2000 x 0.03 = 90 m3/day.

items.q: For a field the rainfall erosivity factor is 350, the soil erodibility factor is 0.35, the combined slope factor is 4, the cover and management factor is 0.15 and the support practice factor is 0.5. Calculate the estimated annual soil loss in tonnes per hectare.
items.s: Soil loss = R x K x LS x C x P = 350 x 0.35 x 4 x 0.15 x 0.5 = 36.75 tonnes per hectare per year.

items.q: The slope length factor of a field is calculated as (slope length/reference length) raised to the power 0.4, where the reference length is 20 m. For a slope length of 30 m, calculate the slope length factor.
items.s: Slope length factor = (30/20)^0.4 = 1.18.

items.q: A catchment of 8 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.3 and the design rainfall intensity for its time of concentration is 75 mm/h. Calculate the peak discharge by the rational method in m3/s.
items.s: Peak discharge = C x i x A/360 = 0.3 x 75 x 8/360 = 0.5 m3/s.

items.q: A drainage system must remove 10 mm of water from 6 hectares within 24 hours. Calculate the required discharge in litres per second.
items.s: Volume = 0.01 m x 60000 m2 = 600 m3, so discharge = 600 m3/(24 x 3600 s) = 6.94 litres per second.

items.q: A grassed waterway has a Manning coefficient of 0.05, a hydraulic radius of 0.5 m and a bed slope of 0.01. Calculate the flow velocity in m/s.
A farmer needs to store 450 m3 of water from a catchment that receives 350 mm of rain a year, with a runoff efficiency of 0.8. Calculate the catchment area needed in hectares.
items.s: Yield per hectare = 0.35 m x 0.8 = 0.28 m3, so area = 450/0.28 = 0.16 hectares = 0.1607.

items.q: A soil core of volume 200 cm3 has an oven dry mass of 352 g. Calculate the bulk density in g/cm3.
items.s: Bulk density = oven dry mass/volume = 352/200 = 1.76 g/cm3.

items.q: A soil has a bulk density of 1.3 g/cm3 and a particle density of 2.65 g/cm3. Calculate its porosity in percent.
items.s: Porosity = (1 - bulk density/particle density) x 100 = (1 - 1.3/2.65) x 100 = 50.9 percent.

items.q: The correct meaning of graded bund is
o: an earth ridge built along the contour to hold water and trap soil
an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet
a small barrier across a gully that slows the flow and traps sediment
the distance measured along the ground between successive conservation ridges
items.s: graded bund: an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet. The other options describe check dam, contour bund, horizontal spacing.

items.q: “a small excavated or embanked reservoir that stores runoff for later use” is the definition of
o: farm pond
seepage
water harvesting
hydraulic radius
items.s: farm pond is a small excavated or embanked reservoir that stores runoff for later use.

items.q: The correct meaning of riser is
o: the reshaping of a field surface to a planned slope by cutting and filling
the gutter along a terrace bench that carries away excess water
the height left between the design water level and the top of an embankment
the steep face between one terrace bench and the next
items.s: riser: the steep face between one terrace bench and the next. The other options describe land grading, freeboard, terrace channel.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines void ratio?
o: the oven dry mass of soil divided by the total volume it occupies, pores included
a compacted layer in the soil that roots and water penetrate only with difficulty
the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay in a soil mass
the volume of voids in a soil divided by the volume of its solid particles
items.s: void ratio: the volume of voids in a soil divided by the volume of its solid particles. The other options describe hardpan, bulk density, soil texture.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines root zone depth?
o: the mass of water held in a soil expressed as a percentage of the oven dry mass of that soil
the moisture left in a soil after free drainage has ceased following thorough wetting
the water held between field capacity and the wilting point that a crop can use
the depth of soil through which the roots of a crop draw their water
items.s: root zone depth: the depth of soil through which the roots of a crop draw their water. The other options describe available water, gravimetric moisture content, field capacity.

items.q: “tillage that leaves crop residue on the surface to shield the soil” is the definition of
o: slope length factor
soil erodibility factor
conservation tillage
rainfall erosivity factor
items.s: conservation tillage is tillage that leaves crop residue on the surface to shield the soil.

items.q: The correct meaning of hydrograph is
o: the part of stream flow that comes from ground water rather than direct storm runoff
the fraction of the rainfall on a catchment that appears as surface flow
a plot of the rate of flow at a point against time
the rainfall event of stated size and duration chosen for the design of a structure
items.s: hydrograph: a plot of the rate of flow at a point against time. The other options describe design storm, base flow, runoff coefficient.

items.q: “the reshaping of a field surface to a planned slope by cutting and filling” is the definition of
o: land grading
cut and fill
terrace channel
terrace
items.s: land grading is the reshaping of a field surface to a planned slope by cutting and filling.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines soil loss equation?
o: a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss where conservation works are in place
the product of climate, soil, slope, cover and practice factors used to estimate long term average erosion
a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss according to the crop and its residue
a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the length of uninterrupted slope increases
items.s: soil loss equation: the product of climate, soil, slope, cover and practice factors used to estimate long term average erosion. The other options describe cover and management factor, slope length factor, support practice factor.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines wind erosion?
o: the removal of a thin fairly uniform layer of soil over a whole slope
the mass of eroded soil that actually leaves a catchment in a stated period
the lifting, sorting and carrying away of dry loose soil by moving air
the susceptibility of a soil to being detached and carried away by erosive agents
items.s: wind erosion: the lifting, sorting and carrying away of dry loose soil by moving air. The other options describe sediment yield, sheet erosion, erodibility.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains volumetric moisture content.
o: the volume of water held in a soil expressed as a fraction of the total soil volume
the mass of water held in a soil expressed as a percentage of the oven dry mass of that soil
the water held between field capacity and the wilting point that a crop can use
moisture held so tightly by soil particles that plants cannot absorb it
items.s: volumetric moisture content: the volume of water held in a soil expressed as a fraction of the total soil volume. The other options describe hygroscopic water, gravimetric moisture content, available water.

items.q: “the spreading of plant material over the soil surface to absorb raindrop energy and hold moisture” is the definition of
o: soil erodibility factor
cover and management factor
mulching
support practice factor
items.s: mulching is the spreading of plant material over the soil surface to absorb raindrop energy and hold moisture.

items.q: The correct meaning of waterlogging is
o: the depth of water that enters the soil in unit time
the ease with which water moves through a soil under a pressure difference
the downward movement of water through the soil body below the surface layer
the condition in which the pore space of the root zone stays filled with water
items.s: waterlogging: the condition in which the pore space of the root zone stays filled with water. The other options describe permeability, infiltration rate, percolation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines graded bund?
o: an earth ridge built along the contour to hold water and trap soil
the height difference between one conservation ridge and the next down the slope
an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet
ploughing along the contour so that each furrow checks the downslope movement of water
items.s: graded bund: an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet. The other options describe vertical interval, contour bund, contour ploughing.

items.q: subsurface drainage may be defined as
o: the depth of water that a drainage system is designed to remove in a stated time
the removal of excess water from within the soil by buried conduits or trenches
the upper surface of the zone in which the soil pores are full of water
the point at which a drain discharges its water into a natural stream or channel
items.s: subsurface drainage: the removal of excess water from within the soil by buried conduits or trenches. The other options describe outlet, water table, drainage coefficient.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines soil loss tolerance?
o: the lifting, sorting and carrying away of dry loose soil by moving air
the greatest rate of erosion that a soil can suffer without losing productivity
the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow
the susceptibility of a soil to being detached and carried away by erosive agents
items.s: soil loss tolerance: the greatest rate of erosion that a soil can suffer without losing productivity. The other options describe wind erosion, rill erosion, erodibility.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an earth ridge built along the contour to hold water and trap soil”
o: horizontal spacing
contour bund
contour line
grassed waterway
items.s: contour bund is an earth ridge built along the contour to hold water and trap soil.

items.q: The correct meaning of conservation tillage is
o: a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the length of uninterrupted slope increases
a value showing how readily a particular soil is lost under a standard set of conditions
a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss according to the crop and its residue
tillage that leaves crop residue on the surface to shield the soil
items.s: conservation tillage: tillage that leaves crop residue on the surface to shield the soil. The other options describe cover and management factor, soil erodibility factor, slope length factor.

items.q: “the part of stream flow that comes from ground water rather than direct storm runoff” is the definition of
o: runoff
design storm
rainfall intensity
base flow
items.s: base flow is the part of stream flow that comes from ground water rather than direct storm runoff.

items.q: The correct meaning of base flow is
o: the area of land from which all surface water drains to a single point
the part of stream flow that comes from ground water rather than direct storm runoff
the part of rainfall that flows over the ground surface instead of entering the soil
the greatest rate of flow reached at a point during or after a storm
items.s: base flow: the part of stream flow that comes from ground water rather than direct storm runoff. The other options describe catchment, runoff, peak discharge.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a row or belt of trees planted to slow the wind over nearby land”
o: evaporation pan
shelterbelt
hydraulic radius
wetted perimeter
items.s: shelterbelt is a row or belt of trees planted to slow the wind over nearby land.

items.q: “the removal of excess water from within the soil by buried conduits or trenches” is the definition of
o: subsurface drainage
water table
drain gradient
surface drainage
items.s: subsurface drainage is the removal of excess water from within the soil by buried conduits or trenches.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cover and management factor.
o: a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss according to the crop and its residue
a multiplier that raises the estimated soil loss as the length of uninterrupted slope increases
a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss where conservation works are in place
the product of climate, soil, slope, cover and practice factors used to estimate long term average erosion
items.s: cover and management factor: a multiplier that reduces estimated soil loss according to the crop and its residue. The other options describe support practice factor, soil loss equation, slope length factor.

items.q: In this course, time of concentration refers to
o: the time taken for water to travel from the farthest point of a catchment to its outlet
the area of land from which all surface water drains to a single point
the greatest rate of flow reached at a point during or after a storm
the rainfall event of stated size and duration chosen for the design of a structure
items.s: time of concentration: the time taken for water to travel from the farthest point of a catchment to its outlet. The other options describe catchment, peak discharge, design storm.

items.q: erosivity may be defined as
o: the removal of a thin fairly uniform layer of soil over a whole slope
the power of rain or wind to detach and transport soil
the cutting of small channels by water that has gathered into threads of flow
the enlargement of rills into deep channels that cannot be crossed by farm machinery
items.s: erosivity: the power of rain or wind to detach and transport soil. The other options describe sheet erosion, rill erosion, gully erosion.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines vertical interval?
o: an earth ridge laid at a slight slope so that excess water drains to a safe outlet
an earth ridge built along the contour to hold water and trap soil
the height difference between one conservation ridge and the next down the slope
ploughing along the contour so that each furrow checks the downslope movement of water
items.s: vertical interval: the height difference between one conservation ridge and the next down the slope. The other options describe contour ploughing, graded bund, contour bund.

items.q: In this course, drain gradient refers to
o: an unlined channel drawn through the subsoil by a bullet shaped implement
the fall of a drain along its length expressed as a ratio or percentage
the removal of water that stands on or flows over the land surface
the removal of excess water from within the soil by buried conduits or trenches
items.s: drain gradient: the fall of a drain along its length expressed as a ratio or percentage. The other options describe mole drain, surface drainage, subsurface drainage.

items.q: The correct meaning of land drainage is
o: the point at which a drain discharges its water into a natural stream or channel
the distance between parallel field drains
the fall of a drain along its length expressed as a ratio or percentage
the removal of surplus water from the soil so that crops can grow
items.s: land drainage: the removal of surplus water from the soil so that crops can grow. The other options describe drain gradient, outlet, drain spacing.

items.q: “the average number of years between storms that equal or exceed a stated size” is the definition of
o: rainfall intensity
return period
base flow
time of concentration
items.s: return period is the average number of years between storms that equal or exceed a stated size.

items.q: In this course, particle density refers to
o: the shade of a soil used as an indicator of drainage, organic matter and mineral content
the arrangement of individual soil particles into groups or aggregates
the mass of the solid particles of a soil divided by the volume of those solids alone
the vertical arrangement of distinct layers seen in a cut through the soil
items.s: particle density: the mass of the solid particles of a soil divided by the volume of those solids alone. The other options describe soil profile, soil colour, soil structure.

items.q: In this course, sediment delivery ratio refers to
o: the removal of a thin fairly uniform layer of soil over a whole slope
the fraction of the soil eroded within a catchment that reaches its outlet
the power of rain or wind to detach and transport soil
